description: An introduction to word processing software used to create, edit, format, save and print text documents on a computer.

options.text: A program used to create and edit text documents
A device that cools the processor inside the computer
A program used only for performing calculations
A tool used to scan documents into pictures

mcq.explanation: A word processor is application software used to type, edit, format, save and print text-based documents.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a word processing program?
mcq.explanation: Microsoft Word is one of the most widely used word processing programs.

mcq.questionText: Which formatting feature makes selected text appear darker and thicker?
mcq.explanation: The bold feature increases the thickness of text to make it stand out.

mcq.questionText: Which command is used to remove selected text and place it on the clipboard so it can be moved elsewhere?
mcq.explanation: Cut removes the selected text from its location and stores it on the clipboard for pasting elsewhere.

mcq.questionText: Which keyboard shortcut is commonly used to save a document?
mcq.explanation: Ctrl + S is the standard shortcut for saving the current document.

mcq.questionText: Which alignment places text evenly along both the left and right margins?
mcq.explanation: Justified text is spaced so that it touches both the left and right margins evenly.

mcq.questionText: What does the spell check feature in a word processor do?

options.text: Changes the colour of the text automatically
Checks the document for spelling mistakes
Saves the document to the clipboard

mcq.explanation: Spell check identifies misspelled words and usually suggests corrections.

mcq.questionText: Which keyboard shortcut is used to copy selected text?
mcq.explanation: Ctrl + C copies the selected text to the clipboard without removing it.

mcq.questionText: Which feature is used to undo the most recent action in a document?
mcq.explanation: The undo command reverses the last action you performed, using Ctrl + Z.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is used to organise data into rows and columns within a document?
mcq.explanation: A table arranges information into rows and columns to make it easier to read.

mcq.questionText: Which formatting feature draws a line beneath selected text?
mcq.explanation: Underline places a horizontal line under the selected text to emphasise it.

mcq.questionText: Which command would you use to make a copy of a document on paper?
mcq.explanation: The print command sends the document to a printer to produce a hard copy on paper.

mcq.questionText: What is the term for the style and design of the characters used in a document, such as Times New Roman or Arial?
mcq.explanation: A font is the particular design of the characters; examples include Times New Roman and Arial.

mcq.questionText: Which shortcut key combination is used to paste text from the clipboard?
mcq.explanation: Ctrl + V pastes the content currently stored on the clipboard into the document.

mcq.questionText: When you want to begin working on a document you created and saved last week, which command should you use?
mcq.explanation: The Open command is used to retrieve and display a document that was previously saved.

fib.questionText: A word processor is a type of application _____ used to create and edit text documents.
fib.explanation: A word processor is application software, meaning a program that performs a specific task for the user.

fib.questionText: The keyboard shortcut Ctrl + Z is used to _____ the last action.
fib.explanation: Ctrl + Z reverses the most recent action carried out in the document.

fib.questionText: Text that is slanted to the right for emphasis is said to be in _____ style.
fib.explanation: Italic formatting slants the characters to the right to give emphasis.

fib.questionText: The _____ command stores text on the clipboard without removing it from its original position.
fib.explanation: Copy duplicates the selected text onto the clipboard while leaving the original in place.

fib.questionText: A temporary storage area that holds cut or copied text until it is pasted is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The clipboard temporarily holds cut or copied content ready to be pasted.

fib.questionText: The small dots or symbols placed in front of items in a list are called _____.
fib.explanation: Bullets are markers used to list items that have no particular order.

fib.questionText: Saving a document for the first time usually requires you to give it a _____.
fib.explanation: When saving a new document you must provide a file name so it can be identified and reopened.

fib.questionText: A printed copy of a document on paper is known as a _____ copy.
fib.explanation: A hard copy is the physical, printed version of a document, while a soft copy is stored electronically.

fib.questionText: Information arranged in rows and columns inside a document is presented using a _____.
fib.explanation: A table organises data into rows and columns for clear presentation.

fib.questionText: The blank spaces around the edges of a page in a document are called _____.
fib.explanation: Margins are the empty spaces between the text and the edges of the page.

tf.questionText: A word processor can be used to type, edit and print text documents.
tf.explanation: Creating, editing and printing text documents are the main uses of a word processor.

tf.questionText: Microsoft Word is an example of a word processing program.
tf.explanation: Microsoft Word is one of the most popular word processing programs.

tf.questionText: The Cut command keeps the selected text in its original place.
tf.explanation: Cut removes the text from its original place; it is Copy that leaves the original unchanged.

tf.questionText: The keyboard shortcut Ctrl + P is used to print a document.
tf.explanation: Ctrl + P opens the print dialog so the document can be sent to the printer.

tf.questionText: Spell check can never make mistakes and always finds every error in a document.
tf.explanation: Spell check is helpful but may miss correctly spelled words used in the wrong way, so the user should still proofread.

tf.questionText: You can insert a picture into a document created with a word processor.
tf.explanation: Word processors allow pictures and other images to be inserted into documents.

tf.questionText: Bold formatting makes text appear thinner and lighter than normal.
tf.explanation: Bold makes text appear darker and thicker, not thinner and lighter.

tf.questionText: Once a document has been saved, it can be opened again later for further editing.
tf.explanation: Saving stores the document so it can be reopened and edited at any time.

tf.questionText: Center alignment positions text along the right margin only.
tf.explanation: Center alignment places text in the middle of the line, equally between the left and right margins.

tf.questionText: Pressing Ctrl + V pastes content that is stored on the clipboard.
tf.explanation: Ctrl + V inserts the clipboard content into the document at the cursor position.

summary.correctAnswer: Software for creating, editing, formatting and printing text documents.
summary.explanation: It is one of the most common types of application software.
Other examples include LibreOffice Writer and Google Docs.

summary.questionText: Main uses of a word processor
summary.correctAnswer: Typing letters, reports, notes and other text documents.
summary.explanation: It also allows formatting and printing of these documents.

summary.correctAnswer: To store a document so it can be opened and used again later.
summary.explanation: The shortcut for saving is Ctrl + S.

summary.correctAnswer: Cut removes text, while Copy duplicates it.
summary.explanation: Both place the text on the clipboard for pasting.

summary.questionText: Purpose of the spell check feature
summary.correctAnswer: To find and help correct spelling mistakes in a document.
summary.explanation: It often suggests the correct spelling of words.

summary.questionText: Common keyboard shortcuts in word processing
summary.correctAnswer: Ctrl + C copy, Ctrl + V paste, Ctrl + X cut, Ctrl + Z undo, Ctrl + S save.
summary.explanation: Shortcuts make working faster than using the menus.

summary.questionText: Use of a table in a document
summary.correctAnswer: To arrange information neatly in rows and columns.
summary.explanation: Tables make data easier to read and compare.
Alignment controls how text is positioned between the margins.

hoq.questionText: A student typed a one-page report, applied bold to the heading, and then realised the whole heading was accidentally deleted. Which single action would most quickly bring the heading back exactly as it was?

options.text: Pressing Ctrl + Z to undo the deletion
Re-typing the heading and applying bold again
Closing the document without saving and reopening it
Pressing Ctrl + P to print the document

hoq.explanation: Undo (Ctrl + Z) reverses the last action, so it restores the deleted heading instantly with its formatting intact.

hoq.questionText: A teacher wants to move a whole paragraph from the end of a document to the beginning without typing it again. Which sequence of commands best achieves this?

options.text: Copy the paragraph, then Paste it at the beginning
Cut the paragraph, place the cursor at the beginning, then Paste
Underline the paragraph, then Save the document
Undo the paragraph, then Redo it at the beginning

hoq.explanation: Cut removes the paragraph and stores it, and Paste inserts it at the new position, so it is moved rather than duplicated.

hoq.questionText: A document passes the spell check with no errors, yet the sentence 'I want to by a new book' is still wrong. Why did spell check fail to catch this mistake?

options.text: Spell check only works on headings, not on sentences
The word 'by' is spelled correctly even though it is the wrong word for the sentence
The document was not saved before running spell check
Spell check cannot run unless a table is inserted first

hoq.explanation: Spell check only flags words it does not recognise; 'by' is a real word, so it is not flagged even though 'buy' was intended, which is why proofreading is still needed.
